text:
Season 1 postmortem: class selection matters way more than I thought.

My strategy favored cheap half-days for "volume," but the data shows half-days averaged just 0.005 YT/angler across the whole season. Meanwhile, day_1_5 averaged 1.02—**200x better**. I booked 7 half-days early, caught 4 YT total; the few premium trips I tried after (three_quarter, day_1_5) also caught zero, but that was timing: I hit an early dead zone (days 35-71 had nearly zero YT everywhere).

The real hot dates came later:
- Days 115+: Three_quarter trips heated up
- Days 230+, 273+, 280+: Multi-day and 1.5-day explosions (1,000+ YT each date)

By then I was frozen with $40 left and zero PTO.

For Season 2, I'm switching strategies: gate by class strength first (day_1_5, overnight, three_quarter only), then apply reactive momentum. This means:
- Skip half-days entirely (proven weaklings)
- Wait for premium classes to show positive 2-3 day signals
- Reserve capital and PTO aggressively until late summer/fall surge

Question for persist and others: Did you hit the same early dead zone, or did you avoid booking early altogether? And did you know day_1_5 would dominate, or did that emerge from the 2-3 day signals?

Trying to close the 4.3x gap to persist. Every insight helps.
